After that: total square footage, the number of separate panes, since ten small windows cost more labor than one big one, shape and access, whether old film has to be stripped first, and whether your glass type forces a higher-spec product. Ask for the film brand and product number in writing.
### Q. Is residential window tinting worth it?
A.  It turns mostly on the glass you already have. On original single-pane windows — common across the city of St. Louis, where 56.1 percent of housing units predate 1940 per the 2024 American Community Survey — film has real room to work, and LBNL’s St. Louis modeling put simple payback on single clear glass at roughly 7 to 11 years. On newer low-e double-pane, most of the solar work is already done and the payback stretches past 20 years.
### Q. Is tinting your home windows a good idea?
A.  It is a good idea when you can name the specific problem it solves. A room you cannot use at 5 p.m., glare that ruins a television, a hardwood floor bleaching by the patio door, a bathroom that needs daytime privacy — film handles all of those well. It is a poor idea if you are buying it purely to cut a utility bill, or if you have not first confirmed your window warranty and glass type.
### Q. What are the window tint rules in Missouri?
A.  Missouri’s tint law is a motor vehicle law, not a building rule. Section 307.173 RSMo sits in the Motor Vehicles title and sets 35 percent light transmission, plus or minus 3 percent, for front side windows. Illinois does the same thing in its Vehicle Code at 625 ILCS 5/12-503, allowing 50 percent on front sides under stated conditions. Neither state limits how dark you tint your house — your HOA or historic district might.
### Q. Where can I get my home windows tinted in St. Louis?
A.  Look for architectural rather than automotive specialists, since the IWFA tests those as separate accreditation tracks. Search a local directory for home window tinting across both Missouri and Illinois sides of the metro, then shortlist on three things: they ask what glass you have before quoting, they hand you the film manufacturer’s written glass breakage and seal failure warranty, and they put the film brand and product number on the estimate.

## How Much Should You Expect to Pay for Framing in St. Louis?
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/blog/what-custom-framing-costs-in-st-louis
Imagine it’s a Saturday morning and you’re standing at a framing counter in Ladue with a rolled-up print under your arm. Or you’re in Bridgeton holding a signed jersey that has lived folded in a closet since 2011. Maybe it’s a photograph of your grandmother that came out of a box in Hanley Hills after the estate sale, curled at the corners, the only copy anyone has.
You already know how this goes. The framer measures, asks a few questions, starts pulling corner samples off the wall, and somewhere in the next ten minutes a number arrives that is three or four times what you had in your head. Then you do what almost everybody does. You smile, say you’ll think about it, and drive home with the piece still in the tube.
Here’s the useful part. That number isn’t arbitrary, and it isn’t really one number — it’s four or five separate decisions stacked on top of each other, and you control most of them. Once you can see which decisions are the expensive ones, and which ones are actually worth paying for, the quote stops being a shock and starts being a menu.
### How much should I expect to pay for framing?
Expect the quote to scale with three things: the size of the finished package, the grade of the glazing, and the grade of the mat. It does not scale with what the picture is worth to you. The same 16x20 print can be framed three legitimate ways with a wide spread between the cheapest version and the most protective one, and the shop is not padding the difference — the materials genuinely cost that much more.
You will notice this article doesn’t print a dollar range. That’s deliberate. Custom framing is priced per shop, per moulding, per project, and moulding costs move with import pricing and freight, so a published range is stale by next quarter and wrong across the river anyway. What you can learn instead is the arithmetic happening behind the counter, so you can read your own quote and see which line item is driving it.
One number in this whole category is published and dated, and it’s worth knowing as a floor: Michaels announced a 10-minute custom framing service on November 18, 2025 — a digital photo printed, framed, and gift boxed for $29, in an 8x8 or 8x10, with four frame finishes and an optional mat. That is a packaged product, not a custom quote. It tells you what the cheap end of a gift photo looks like. It tells you nothing about your grandmother’s portrait.
### What are you actually paying for?
A framing quote is built from four buckets: moulding measured by the foot, mat and backing measured in united inches, glazing measured by area, and labor. Understanding the four is what lets you negotiate. You can’t argue a shop down on glass, but you can absolutely redesign the mat.
Moulding by the foot. Frame shops buy moulding in lengths from distributors and price it per foot. Here’s the part customers never expect: the footage you need is not the perimeter of your picture. Because all four corners are mitered, the trade formula adds eight times the moulding width to the perimeter. A 16x20 opening has a 72-inch perimeter, but in a 2-inch-wide moulding it consumes 32 + 40 + 16 = 88 inches, or about 7 feet 4 inches. So a wider frame costs you twice: more dollars per foot, and more feet.
United inches. This is the industry’s shorthand for size — one long side plus one short side. A 16x20 is 36 united inches. Mats, backing, fitting and a lot of the labor line are priced off that single figure, which is why shops can quote so fast once they know your dimensions.
Glazing by area. Glass and acrylic are priced from sheets, so glazing cost tracks square inches, not united inches. This is the reason big pieces jump in price faster than they look like they should.
Labor and fitting. Cutting the mat opening with a beveled edge, joining and clamping the corners, mounting or hinging the artwork, cleaning the glazing, fitting everything into the rabbet, sealing the back with a dust cover, and attaching hardware. Hobby Lobby’s own custom framing page describes the package the same way: the moulding, the matting, protective glass, an acid-free dust cover on the back, and the hangers needed to mount it.
### How much does it cost to frame a 24x36 picture?
There’s no honest single number, but there is a very clear reason a 24x36 quote lands so much higher than a 16x20 one: it is a step change, not a proportional increase. Run the arithmetic and you can see exactly where the money goes.
A 16x20 is 36 united inches and 320 square inches of glass. A 24x36 is 60 united inches and 864 square inches. So the size figure the mat and labor are priced from rises about 67 percent, while the glazing area rises about 170 percent. That alone explains a lot of the gap.
Now add a 3-inch mat all the way around, which is a normal design choice at that scale. Your outside dimension becomes 30x42 — 72 united inches and 1,260 square inches, nearly four times the glazing area of that 16x20. In a 2-inch moulding, the footage goes from about 7 feet 4 inches to 13 feet 4 inches.
And there’s a hard break you should know about. A standard full sheet of mat board is 32x40 inches. A 30x42 outside dimension does not fit on one, so the shop has to move to jumbo board, commonly 40x60. That is a genuine material step, not a markup. If your budget is tight on a large piece, the single most effective thing you can do is design the mat so the outside dimension stays inside 32x40 — a 2-inch mat instead of a 3-inch mat on a 24x36 keeps you at 28x40 and on a standard sheet.
At that size the glazing conversation changes too. A sheet of glass over 1,200 square inches is heavy and genuinely dangerous if it lets go on the stairs, so many shops steer large work to acrylic, which weighs roughly half as much as glass and won’t break into shards.
### Which choices actually move the number?
Glazing and mat grade move it most, and both are real value rather than upsell. Everything else — a fancier moulding, a second mat, a v-groove, a fabric wrap — is taste, and taste is where you cut if you have to.
Glazing tiers. The spread here is enormous and the labels are slippery, so ask for the actual specification. Tru Vue, the dominant glazing manufacturer in the trade, lists its non-conservation Premium Clear glass at 45 percent UV protection. Its Conservation Clear line blocks up to 99 percent of UV, with more than 89 percent light transmission and about 8 percent reflection. Its Museum Glass blocks up to 99 percent of UV and adds the anti-reflective coating — less than 1 percent reflection and more than 97 percent light transmission. The manufacturer states its conservation-grade products meet ISO 18902 and pass ISO 18916, the photographic activity test. If a shop says only “UV glass,” that could mean 45 percent or it could mean 99. Make them say which.
Mat grade. A decorative paper-faced mat, a conservation mat made of purified alpha-cellulose, and a museum mat of 100 percent cotton rag are three different products at three different prices. Cotton is naturally acid-free and needs the least chemical processing, which is why museums default to it. Alpha-cellulose conservation board is the sensible middle, and it is what most people should buy for anything they care about.
Float mounting. Floating a piece so the deckled or torn edges show, instead of covering them with a mat window, means the artwork sits on top of the board rather than under it. That requires spacers to hold the glazing off the surface, which adds depth and a step of labor. It looks fantastic on hand-torn paper and it costs more.
Mounting method. Dry mounting bonds the piece to a board with heat and adhesive. It is flat, it is cheap, and it is permanent. Hinging with Japanese paper and wheat starch paste is the conservation alternative, and the paste releases with moisture, which is the entire point. For a poster, dry mount it. For anything signed, numbered, original, or irreplaceable, do not.
Oversize. Past 32x40 you are in jumbo materials, and past that you are into shipping considerations and acrylic. Ask where the price breaks are before you fall in love with a mat width.
Nothing to do with frames — lawn and garden help.
### What does archival or conservation framing actually mean?
It means every material touching your piece is chemically stable, and every step taken today can be undone tomorrow without damaging the artwork. Reversibility is the real test, not the word on the sticker. “Acid-free” only describes the pH of a board at the moment it was made; it says nothing about what that board does in twenty years inside a sealed frame.
The Northeast Document Conservation Center’s preservation leaflet on matting and framing works on paper describes the standard: a window and backboard of 4-ply 100 percent ragboard or lignin-free archival board, with the object attached to the backboard using hinges of Japanese paper and wheat starch paste, or with corner supports and edge strips that put no adhesive on the object at all. Wheat starch paste can be removed with moisture. That is why conservators use it.
The second half of conservation framing is the air gap. Nothing should press against the glazing. A mat creates that gap automatically; a float mount needs spacers to do the same job. This matters more here than in a dry climate, because a St. Louis August moves a lot of moisture through a house, and a photographic emulsion held tight against glass through enough humid summers can bond to it. Separating them again is a conservation job, not a framing job.
Buffering is the last wrinkle. Buffered board carries an alkaline reserve that absorbs acidic gases from inside the frame, including from wood mouldings, which are themselves acidic. Some photographic processes do better on unbuffered board. If you are framing photographs, say the word “photographs” out loud and let the framer pick.
One honest limit: UV glazing filters ultraviolet light, not visible light, and visible light fades things too. Conservation glass buys years, not immunity. Nothing you care about should hang where afternoon sun lands on it, which is why the cheapest preservation upgrade in most houses isn’t glass at all — it’s a blind or a shade on the window, or a UV-blocking film on the glass itself.
### Where is the cheapest place to get custom framing?
The cheapest framing is the framing you don’t buy custom. If your piece is already a standard size — 5x7, 8x10, 11x14, 16x20, 18x24, 24x36 — a ready-made frame and a pre-cut mat will beat any custom quote by a wide margin, and for a reproduction poster that is the correct answer, not a compromise.
Four more ways to move the number down without wrecking the result:
Let the mat do the fitting. If your piece is an odd size but close to a standard, buy a ready-made frame at the nearest standard size and pay only for a custom-cut mat. That is often the single biggest saving available.
Print to a standard size. If you are having a photo printed anyway, size the file to a standard frame before you print it, not after.
Bring your own frame. Most shops will fit new mat, glazing and backing into a frame you already own. Ask. If a moulding you love turns up at an estate sale in Webster Groves, it may be worth more to you than the sample corner on the wall.
Spend the savings on glazing. If you have to choose, a plain moulding with conservation glass protects your piece. An ornate moulding with 45 percent UV glass does not.
And read the discount carefully. Hobby Lobby’s custom framing page states that custom frames are 50 percent off the marked price and that the discount applies to frames only. That is a real saving on one of the four buckets. It is not 50 percent off your ticket, and two quotes carrying the same headline percentage can still land far apart.
### Is Hobby Lobby or Michaels cheaper for picture frames?
Nobody can answer that honestly as a blanket yes or no, and this article isn’t going to pretend otherwise. Both chains price custom work per project, both run promotional structures that change what a shelf number means, and neither publishes a comparable price list you could hold side by side. Anyone declaring a winner is guessing or selling something.
What can be verified is what each says about its own service. Hobby Lobby’s custom framing page says there is a framing expert in every store, that custom frames are 50 percent off the marked price for frames only, that the package includes moulding, matting, protective glass, an acid-free dust cover and hangers, and that UV-protective glass is standard with museum glass and cotton rag mats available. Michaels announced its 10-minute service for printed photos on November 18, 2025, at $29, in more than 500 stores at launch with a chainwide rollout by February 2026.
Rather than chasing a winner, compare the seven things that actually differ between any two framing counters, chain or independent:
Who cuts the mat, and where. Cut on site, or ordered from a central production facility? This drives turnaround more than anything else.
Does your piece leave the building? For a replaceable poster, who cares. For the only photograph of your grandmother, that is the whole question.
Which glazing lines are stocked. Ask for the UV percentage, not the adjective.
What mounting is the default. Is hinging offered, or is dry mounting simply what happens?
Will they refit a frame you already own? Some will, some won’t.
Can they handle the unusual piece? A jersey needs sewing, not adhesive. A shadow box needs depth. A diploma with a raised seal needs a spacer.
Turnaround, in writing. Especially in May and December.
Broadly, the independent shop’s advantage is the design conversation and the odd job; the chain’s advantage is convenience and visible discounting. Which of those is worth more depends entirely on what is in your hands. Get an itemized quote from both on identical specifications and the comparison answers itself.
### Does the Missouri or the Illinois side change what you pay?
Barely, and probably not enough to drive for. A finished framed piece is tangible goods, taxed at the shop’s address. Missouri’s state sales tax rate is 4.225 percent; Illinois charges 6.25 percent on general merchandise. Local add-ons close most of that gap: the Tax Foundation’s 2026 figures put the average combined state and local rate near 8.44 percent in Missouri and about 8.75 percent in Illinois.
On a $600 framing job, roughly three tenths of a percentage point is under two dollars. Meanwhile a single address in the city of St. Louis can sit well above the Missouri average, and a Belleville or Edwardsville shop can come in under the Illinois average. The rate that matters is the one at the counter you are standing at, and both states publish address-level lookup tools — the Missouri Department of Revenue rate map and the Illinois Tax Rate Finder.
The differences worth caring about are practical, not fiscal. Turnaround, in-house work and whether anyone there will touch a jersey vary far more between two shops in the same county than between the two states.
### What the person on the other side of the counter is watching
A frame shop is a custom manufacturer with a retail front, and the arithmetic is unforgiving. Moulding is bought by the foot, and miter waste is real — that 16x20 in a 2-inch profile eats 88 inches of stick, not the 72 the perimeter suggests, and the drop usually can’t be sold to anybody. Output is capped by one bench, one mat cutter and one pair of hands, so a shop can only finish so many pieces in a day no matter how hard the phone rings. The year is lumpy too: graduation season in May and the holiday run in the fall carry months that are much quieter. And the thing framers say to each other is that percentage-off signage down the road resets what a fair price sounds like before they have opened their mouth. The good ones answer it by showing the work — naming the board, naming the UV number, saying out loud whether the mounting can be undone. Which is also why being findable matters: people search this trade the week they need it, and a complete listing is how a shop gets into that search at all.
### How do you get a quote you can actually compare?
Bring the piece, not the measurements — a framer needs to see the paper, the edges and the condition. Then ask for the quote itemized, and take the same list to a second shop. Nine questions do the whole job:
What is the moulding footage, and the price per foot?
What is the mat made of — decorative paper, alpha-cellulose conservation, or 100 percent cotton rag?
What percentage of UV does the glazing block, and what is the product name?
Is the mounting reversible, and what adhesive is used?
Does the outside dimension cross 32x40, and what does that change?
Glass or acrylic, and why for this piece?
Who does the work, in which building, and what is the turnaround?
What happens if the piece is damaged while it is with you?
Does anyone here hold a Certified Picture Framer credential?
That last one is a real thing, not a nicety. The Professional Picture Framers Association has run the Certified Picture Framer exam since 1986, developed with Educational Testing Service — a three-and-a-half-hour written test covering preservation, mounting, mechanics and framing math, with a Master credential above it that requires five years in the trade. Plenty of excellent framers never sat it. But if someone has, they will tell you, and the conversation that follows will be a better one.
Still carrying it around in a cardboard tube? Browse framing shops across the St. Louis metro on St Louis Near Me Directory, then take the same nine questions to two of them and compare the itemized quotes line by line.
If you run a business like this yourself, list your business.
### Frequently asked questions
### Q. Where can I find custom picture framing in St. Louis?
A.  Four kinds of places do it: independent frame shops, galleries and art-supply stores with a framing counter, craft chains with an in-store framing department, and photo labs that sell framed prints. Shortlist two or three, then call and describe your piece — size, condition, and what it actually is — before you drive anywhere.
### Q. Where can I find custom framing services in Saint Louis, Missouri?
A.  Both sides of the river have them, and for an Illinois-side reader a shop in Belleville or Edwardsville is often a shorter trip than crossing into the city. Rather than sorting by distance, call ahead and ask three things: is the mat cut on site, does my piece leave the building, and which glazing lines do you stock?
### Q. Does Hobby Lobby still do framing?
A.  Yes. Hobby Lobby’s custom framing page says there is a framing expert in every store, and describes a package that includes the moulding, matting, protective glass, an acid-free dust cover on the back, and the hangers needed to mount it. The same page lists museum glass and cotton rag mats as options.
### Q. Does Hobby Lobby charge for framing?
A.  Yes — custom framing is a paid service. The advertised 50 percent off applies to the frame, and Hobby Lobby’s own page states the discount is for frames only. Matting, glazing, mounting and fitting labor are priced separately, which is exactly why two quotes carrying the same headline discount can land far apart.
### Q. Why is framing necessary?
A.  For a poster you would happily replace, it isn’t. For anything you can’t replace, it is. A frame holds the piece flat, keeps hands and dust off the surface, and with conservation glazing filters up to 99 percent of the ultraviolet light that fades ink and paper. For an original photograph or a signed item, that protection is the entire purchase.
### Q. Do paintings sell better, framed or unframed?
A.  Nobody publishes a reliable number on this, so treat any confident answer as sales talk. What is verifiable: juried shows publish presentation rules in the artist prospectus, and works on paper generally have to be matted or framed to hang. The Art Fair at Queeny Park, run each spring and fall by the Greater St. Louis Artists Organization, juries more than 120 artists. Read the rules before you spend.
### Q. What are the trends in picture framing for 2026?
A.  The clearest documented shift is speed. Michaels announced 10-minute custom framing on November 18, 2025 — a printed photo, framed and gift boxed, in an 8x8 or 8x10 for $29, in more than 500 stores at launch and chainwide by February 2026. Beyond dated announcements like that, most published trend lists are marketing rather than measured demand.
### Q. Is a framer a good job?
A.  Picture framing is a skilled retail trade — measuring, mat cutting, joining, mounting and preservation decisions, mostly on your feet. There is a real credential behind it: the Professional Picture Framers Association has offered the Certified Picture Framer exam since 1986, developed with Educational Testing Service, with a Master level above it. Pay tracks the shop and the market, not the title.

## How to Pick a Steakhouse in St. Louis
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/blog/how-to-pick-a-steakhouse-in-st-louis
Imagine it’s a Tuesday in October and you have somehow been handed three dinners at once. Your anniversary lands a week from Saturday. Your boss wants a client taken somewhere Thursday that quietly says the company is doing fine. And your father-in-law turns seventy in November and has announced, out loud, that what he wants is a steak.
Three dinners, three completely different rooms. The place in Clayton that would land the client is too stiff for a seventieth birthday. The bar in Jennings that grills the best strip you have eaten all year is not where you raise a glass to thirty years of marriage. And the room your neighbor in Frontenac swears by turns out to be booked solid for anything after 6:30 p.m. for the next two weekends.
Picking a steakhouse is rarely about finding the single best one. It is about matching the room to the night, then reading the menu closely enough that the check does not ambush you. Here is how to do both — the categories, the grading vocabulary, the aging vocabulary, and the money.
### What are the signs of a good quality steak house?
A good steakhouse can answer three questions without hedging: what grade the beef is, how it was aged, and what the wait actually looks like tonight. A staff that dodges all three is telling you something. Past that, the reliable signal is execution rather than decor — the steak comes out at the temperature you asked for, and it comes out that way every visit.
Grade is the easiest tell because it is a federal standard, not a marketing word. USDA’s Agricultural Marketing Service defines Prime as beef from young, well-fed cattle with at least slightly abundant marbling, and says plainly that it is “generally sold in upscale restaurants.” Choice has less marbling than Prime but is still high quality. Select is leaner and, by USDA’s own description, may lack some of the juiciness and flavor of the higher grades. A menu that names its grade has committed to something checkable. A menu that says only “hand-cut” has not.
The other signals are small and they add up. A server who volunteers which cut came in best this week. Sides that taste cooked rather than assembled. A bar that can make a proper old fashioned without looking it up. A host who can tell you, honestly, that 7:15 on Saturday is not happening but 5:30 is wide open. And a kitchen that sends the steak back without argument when it arrives medium and you asked for medium rare. None of that requires white tablecloths.
### What kinds of steakhouse does St. Louis actually have?
Four kinds, and they are not competing for the same night. There are the national chains, the independent white-tablecloth rooms, the old-school supper clubs that never changed, and the neighborhood bar that quietly puts out a very good steak. Deciding which category you want narrows the search faster than any list of names.
The chains are the biggest category by a wide margin. Technomic’s Top 500 data, reported by Restaurant Business on April 3, 2025, put Texas Roadhouse at $5.5 billion in U.S. systemwide sales across 664 restaurants in 2024 — enough to pass Olive Garden and become the largest casual-dining chain in the country. LongHorn Steakhouse, at 594 units, moved ahead of Outback Steakhouse into sixth place among casual-dining brands. What you get is predictability: bundled sides, a posted menu, a waitlist app, and no dress code. For a big family birthday with kids at the table, predictability is the feature.
The independent white-tablecloth rooms are the opposite trade. Smaller menus, steaks priced individually, a real wine list, and a staff that has worked the room long enough to remember you. This is the client-dinner category and the milestone-anniversary category. It is also where the bill needs the most attention before you go, because almost nothing is included.
The supper-club survivors are the ones with the vinyl booths, the relish tray, the iceberg wedge and a salad that arrives whether you asked or not. They tend to be older, family-run, and priced like the 1980s never fully ended. If your father-in-law says he wants a steak and a real dinner, this is usually the category he means, and he is usually right.
Then there is the tavern that does one steak special extremely well — often a strip or a ribeye, often on a chalkboard, often Friday and Saturday only. Metro-east taverns in Belleville and the older bars in Maryland Heights and south county are full of them. It is the best value of the four and the worst choice for an occasion that needs a quiet table. Call first and ask two things: whether the special runs tonight, and whether they take reservations at all.
### How do you read a steakhouse menu?
Read for three things in order: the grade, the aging, and what the cut actually is. Everything else on the page is arrangement. Those three decide what lands on the plate, and all three are things a server can answer in one sentence if the kitchen is confident.
On grading: USDA quality grades run Prime, Choice and Select at the retail end, with Standard and Commercial usually sold ungraded or as store brands. Grading is voluntary — the rules are literally titled Regulations Governing the Voluntary Grading of Meat and Meat Products — so an ungraded steak is not automatically bad, it is simply unlabeled. Two words worth separating: “prime rib” is the name of a cut from the rib primal and says nothing about grade. A prime rib can be USDA Choice. If the menu means the grade, it will say USDA Prime.
On aging, dry and wet are different products, not different quality levels. A 2016 peer-reviewed review in the Journal of Animal Science and Technology describes dry aging as hanging carcasses or primal cuts for 28 to 55 days in a refrigerated room held between roughly 32 and 39 degrees Fahrenheit at 75 to 80 percent relative humidity. The cost is brutal: shrinkage of 6 to 15 percent, trim loss of 3 to 24 percent, and it only works on heavily marbled, high-grade beef. That is why a 45-day dry-aged ribeye costs what it costs, and why it tastes nutty and concentrated rather than simply beefy. Wet aging — vacuum-sealed, no evaporation — is the industry default, keeps more weight, and produces a cleaner, milder steak. Neither is wrong. They are two flavors.
On cuts, “butcher’s cut” is a menu phrase, not a federal one. It usually means either an under-known muscle the kitchen likes or whatever the butcher trimmed out that morning. Ask which muscle it is; a good server will name it. And decide your temperature before the server arrives. USDA’s food safety guidance for whole beef steaks is 145 degrees Fahrenheit internal with a three-minute rest, which is medium; anything rarer is a doneness preference, not a safety standard, and every steakhouse in the metro will cook it that way if you ask.
### Why does a steak cost what it costs right now?
Because there is not much cattle. USDA’s National Agricultural Statistics Service reported on January 30, 2026 that the U.S. herd stood at 86.2 million head as of January 1, the smallest inventory in 75 years, with beef cows down another 1 percent to 27.6 million. Fewer cattle, steady demand, higher prices. That is the whole mechanism, and it has been running for several years.
You can see it at retail. Bureau of Labor Statistics average price data puts USDA Choice boneless sirloin at $14.59 a pound in July 2026, up from $13.55 in July 2025 — about 7.7 percent in a year. Over the same twelve months the BLS index for food away from home rose about 3.4 percent. Restaurant menu prices, in other words, have not kept pace with what the beef itself is doing. That gap is being absorbed somewhere.
Mostly it is being absorbed by the restaurant. Texas Roadhouse, which is public and therefore has to show its work, reported on February 19, 2026 that full-year 2025 commodity inflation ran 6.1 percent and its restaurant margin fell 165 basis points to 15.5 percent of restaurant and other sales. That is a very large, very efficient operator getting squeezed. So when a neighborhood room raises a strip by three dollars, that is not opportunism. It is arithmetic.
Nothing to do with steak — the florists close before your reservation.
### A la carte or included sides — what does that do to the bill?
It roughly doubles it. At a white-tablecloth room the steak price is the steak alone: no potato, no vegetable, sometimes not even a salad. Sides are separate, portioned family-style, and meant to be shared. At a chain or a supper club, a side or two and a salad usually come with the entree. Same-looking entree prices, very different totals.
Do the math before you book, not after. Pull the menu up on the restaurant’s own site and count the lines a table of four will actually order: four entrees, two or three shared sides, a salad or two, drinks. Add the sauce or compound-butter upcharge if there is one, the seafood add-on if anybody wants it, then sales tax and tip. That number is the real per-person cost, and it is frequently close to double the steak line by itself.
Two ways to keep it sane without eating badly. Ask whether there is a prix fixe or a chef’s menu — many rooms run one, and it is often the best value on the page. And consider going at 5:30 on a weeknight instead of 7:30 on Saturday; the same kitchen, the same cuts, a calmer room, and in a fair number of places a better chance at a table you would actually want.
### What is different about a steakhouse on the Illinois side?
Three things you will actually notice: smoking rules, the tax line, and how servers are paid. The Smoke-Free Illinois Act has banned smoking in restaurants, bars and gaming floors statewide since January 1, 2008, so a metro-east steakhouse is smoke-free by law. Missouri is looser. The state Clean Indoor Air Law leaves much of the decision to the owner, and St. Louis County requires a drinking establishment to hold a granted exemption before it can allow indoor smoking. St. Charles County adopted its own Smoke-Free Air Act in 2018.
The tax line differs too. Illinois taxes prepared restaurant food at the state high rate of 6.25 percent plus local taxes, and separately removed the 1 percent state grocery tax on January 1, 2026 while letting municipalities impose their own 1 percent. In Missouri, the reduced 1.225 percent state food rate does not apply at an establishment where food prepared for immediate consumption is more than 80 percent of gross receipts — which is every steakhouse. So restaurant meals get the full rate on both sides of the river; the local add-ons are what move your total.
Server pay is the quiet difference. Missouri’s minimum wage reached $15.00 an hour on January 1, 2026, and tipped employees must be paid at least 50 percent of that — $7.50 — plus whatever brings them to $15.00. Illinois has been at $15.00 since January 1, 2025, with the tip credit capped so a tipped worker’s cash wage runs higher. Practical effect for you: read the bottom of the menu and the bottom of the check. Service charges, large-party gratuities and kitchen fees are showing up more often, and they are not always the same as a tip.
### How do reservations, dress and timing actually work?
Book two to four weeks out for a Saturday between 6:30 and 8:00, and longer for Valentine’s Day, Mother’s Day, graduation weekends and the December party stretch. Those are the dates that fill first at every price level. A Tuesday or a 5:30 seating is often available the same week at the same room.
Say what the night is when you book. Anniversary, birthday, first client dinner — the host writes it down, and it changes which table you get and whether anyone bothers with a candle. Ask for a specific spot if you care: a booth, away from the bar, not under the speaker. Confirm by phone two days ahead, especially if the reservation came through an app. And check the cancellation policy, because more rooms now hold a card and charge for a no-show on a prime-time table.
On dress, call and ask rather than guessing from photos. Very few steakhouses in this metro still require a jacket and almost none require a tie; business casual clears nearly every door, and the chains have no code at all. If you are pairing dinner with a show, build in an hour more than you think you need for parking and the check — our guide to live theater and performing arts in St. Louis covers how those curtain times line up.
### What should you order if you are not a steak person?
Order the seafood, and order it without apology. Most serious steakhouses are half seafood houses — the same broiler, the same butter, and often the kitchen’s best non-beef work. Salmon, scallops, crab, a shrimp cocktail built for two. At the chains, the chicken and the pork chop are usually competent and the burger is frequently the smartest thing on the menu.
The sides are also a legitimate dinner. In a room where everything is shared anyway, a wedge salad, creamed spinach and a baked potato is a real meal and nobody will blink. If you eat vegetarian or vegan, call ahead rather than hoping — some kitchens have a genuine entree ready and some will improvise a plate of sides, and it is much better to know which before you sit down with six people.
One honest piece of ordering advice: if you like your steak well done, do not order the 45-day dry-aged ribeye. You are paying for a texture and a concentration that cook out. Order the filet, the prime rib or the sirloin and enjoy the night. And if the whole idea of a big beef dinner is wrong for the occasion, this town has other answers — start with the dishes this city actually invented.
### What does a steakhouse look like from the owner’s side of the pass?
Beef is the hardest food cost in full-service dining, because you cannot mark up a commodity everybody can price at Schnucks. Texas Roadhouse, a public company with enormous buying power, still watched 6.1 percent commodity inflation cut its 2025 restaurant margin by 165 basis points to 15.5 percent. An independent room has less cushion than that. The margin lives in the bar, the wine list and the shared sides — which is exactly why sides are priced separately and why the bartender is good. The calendar is brutal too: Valentine’s Day, Mother’s Day, graduation weekends and December carry the year, and January is a ghost town. The thing operators grumble about to each other is the same every time — a party of eight calling Friday for Saturday at seven, then a no-show on a table that was turned away four times. Steady bookings from people who found you on purpose are worth more than a busy weekend, and a complete listing on St Louis Near Me Directory is one way people find you on purpose.
If cooking the steak at home starts to sound better than ordering one, it is worth knowing whether a St. Louis butcher is cheaper than the grocery store before you go.
Booking a night that has to go right? Browse steak houses across the St. Louis metro on St Louis Near Me Directory, then call the two you like most and ask each one what a Saturday at 7 p.m. looks like three weeks out.
If you’re the one providing it, get listed.
### Frequently asked questions
### Q. What makes a steak house a steakhouse?
A.  Beef sits at the center of the menu and the kitchen is built around it — a high-heat broiler or grill, whole-muscle cuts portioned in house, and steaks priced individually rather than as a plate. USDA quality grades usually appear on the page. The seafood, the sides and the wine list are all arranged around the steak rather than beside it.
### Q. What is the difference between a steak house and a chop house?
A.  Historically, chophouses came first: London rooms from the 1690s serving individual portions of meat, chops included, to working men. American steakhouses grew out of that tradition in the mid-1800s and narrowed onto beef and occasion dining. Today the two words are used interchangeably on signs, though a chophouse menu often carries more lamb, veal and pork alongside the beef.
### Q. What makes a steak house truly exceptional?
A.  Consistency you would bet an anniversary on. The kitchen hits your temperature every time, the server knows what came in strongest that week, the sides are cooked rather than reheated, and the host can hold a table when your party runs twenty minutes late. Sourcing sets the ceiling, but execution is what separates two rooms charging the same price.
### Q. What are the most popular steakhouse chains?
A.  By U.S. systemwide sales, Texas Roadhouse leads. Technomic Top 500 data reported by Restaurant Business on April 3, 2025 put it at $5.5 billion across 664 restaurants in 2024, making it the largest casual-dining chain in the country, ahead of Olive Garden. LongHorn Steakhouse, with 594 units, moved past Outback Steakhouse into sixth place among casual-dining brands.
### Q. Is Texas Roadhouse considered a steak house?
A.  Yes — a casual-dining steakhouse, and by sales the largest restaurant chain in that segment. Technomic put its 2024 U.S. systemwide sales at $5.5 billion across 664 locations. The distinction people usually mean is between casual steakhouses, where sides come bundled with the entree, and white-tablecloth chophouses, where the steak is priced alone and everything else is separate.
### Q. What is the average cost per person at a steakhouse?
A.  There is no reliable published national average, and the honest range is enormous. What moves your number is menu structure. At a white-tablecloth room the entree price is the steak alone, with sides separate and shared, so the real per-person total often lands near double the entree line once sides, one drink, sales tax and tip are added.
### Q. What is the dress code for a steak house?
A.  Call and ask — every host in this metro will tell you straight. Very few area steakhouses still require a jacket and almost none require a tie. Business casual, meaning a collared shirt with slacks or dark jeans and closed shoes, clears nearly every door. Casual chain steakhouses have no dress code at all.
### Q. What is the proper etiquette at a steakhouse?
A.  Order your steak the way you like it and skip the apology. Sides are usually shared, so agree on them as a table before ordering. Taste before you salt. Let the server tell you what came in well this week. If a steak arrives wrong, say so at the first bite instead of at the end, and tip on the pre-discount total.
### Q. Why are steak houses dark?
A.  Low light is inherited from the 19th-century chophouse — dark wood, deep booths, shaded lamps — and it stuck because it makes a long, expensive dinner feel private. It also flatters the room and the plate. It is a convention rather than a rule; plenty of newer steakhouses are bright, and bar-side steak is usually served under ordinary lights.
### Q. What is the 3-3-3 rule for steaks?
A.  A home-grilling shorthand, not a restaurant standard: sear a one-inch steak about three minutes a side over direct heat, move it to indirect heat for roughly three minutes a side, then rest it. You will also see a 3-3-2-2 version floating around, which tells you it is folk wisdom. USDA’s actual guidance is 145 degrees Fahrenheit internal with a three-minute rest.

## What a Home Appraisal Involves in St. Louis
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/blog/what-a-home-appraisal-involves-in-st-louis
Imagine it’s a Thursday morning in Sunset Hills and your loan officer texts you: the appraiser is coming Monday, somewhere between ten and noon. That’s the whole message. Nobody has told you whether to be home, whether the basement matters, or what happens to your deal if the number lands somewhere you don’t like.
Or you’re the seller in St. Ann who just accepted an offer twelve thousand dollars above what the house two streets over closed for. Or you’re refinancing in Troy, over on the Illinois side, and the lender says the appraisal fee is non-refundable, and you’d like to know what you’re buying. Or you’re settling your mother’s estate, and somebody told you that you need an appraisal and not a market analysis, and you’re not sure those are different things.
They are different things, and the difference is written into state law. So here is the plain version of a residential appraisal in this metro: who orders it, who pays, what the appraiser measures and why, how long it takes, what actually happens when the value lands under the contract price, and where Missouri and Illinois part ways. No promises about your number. Just the process, with the rules that govern it named out loud.
### What is the point of getting a house appraised?
A lender orders an appraisal to confirm the house is worth enough to secure the loan. It protects the lender’s collateral, not your purchase. A credentialed, independent appraiser gives an opinion of market value as of a specific date, and the loan gets underwritten against the lower of that value or your contract price.
HUD says the quiet part out loud in its own paperwork. The FHA Amendatory Clause, in the model document HUD published in March 2023, states that the appraised valuation exists to determine the maximum mortgage HUD will insure, and that HUD does not warrant the value or condition of the property. That is the lender’s appraisal in one sentence: a collateral check, doing a job for somebody else.
Outside of lending you can order one yourself, and the purpose flips. Divorce settlements, date-of-death and estate valuations, a property tax appeal, removing private mortgage insurance, a pre-listing sanity check. In all of those you are the client, you pick the appraiser, and the report answers your question instead of a lender’s.
### Who orders the appraisal, and who pays for it?
Your lender orders it, usually through an appraisal management company, and you pay for it. You do not pick the appraiser, and neither does your agent. That is deliberate: federal valuation independence rules at 12 CFR 1026.42 prohibit anyone with an interest in the transaction from coercing, bribing, or otherwise attempting to influence an appraiser’s opinion of value.
The fee lands on your Loan Estimate under Section B, Services You Cannot Shop For, next to the credit report and the flood determination. That heading is literal. For the rest of the closing table — title, settlement, transfer taxes, prepaids, and which of them Missouri handles differently from Illinois — see what closing costs actually cost in St. Louis. This post stays on the appraisal line.
You are entitled to the report you paid for. Under the Equal Credit Opportunity Act valuations rule at 12 CFR 1002.14, a creditor must give an applicant a copy of every appraisal and written valuation developed for a loan secured by a first lien on a dwelling, promptly on completion and no later than three business days before closing. You can waive the timing. You cannot be charged extra for the copy.
Both states register the middleman. Missouri appraisal management companies register with the Real Estate Appraisers Commission under sections 339.500 to 339.549 RSMo; Illinois AMCs register with the Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation under the Real Estate Appraiser Licensing Act of 2002.
### How much does a home appraisal cost in St. Louis?
No government agency publishes an average for a conventional St. Louis appraisal, so the honest answer starts from a published ceiling. On the VA’s appraisal fee and timeliness table effective May 1, 2026, the maximum allowable single-family appraisal fee is $700 in Missouri and $650 in Illinois.
The rest of that table is worth having. In Missouri the VA caps an individual condominium at $700, a manufactured home at $750, and a two-to-four unit property at $850. The Illinois rows read $650, $700, and $850. Those are ceilings for VA-guaranteed loans, not conventional averages — but they come from a federal agency, they are current, and they cover both sides of the river.
Here is the part to be honest about: no state agency, assessor, or appraiser trade body publishes a conventional appraisal figure for Missouri or Illinois. Cost-comparison sites publish national averages, but those are self-reported and not St. Louis specific, so quoting one as a local price would be inventing precision. The number that binds you sits in Section B of your Loan Estimate, and it moves with complexity: acreage, an odd floor plan, a multi-unit building, a rushed turn time.
### What does the appraiser actually look at?
Three things: your house, the comparable sales, and the market around both. The appraiser measures the exterior, builds a sketch or floor plan, records condition, quality, age, room count and functional problems, then adjusts recent nearby sales up or down for the differences to reach an opinion of value.
The measuring is where St. Louis homeowners get blindsided. For loans sold to Fannie Mae, appraisals requiring interior and exterior inspections with effective dates of April 1, 2022 or later must calculate gross living area using the ANSI Z765-2021 measuring standard. Fannie Mae’s Standardized Property Measuring Guidelines, published July 2022, put it flatly: any space partially or completely below grade is reported as basement area. Finished space counted in gross living area needs a ceiling at least seven feet high, and in a sloped-ceiling room at least half the finished square footage must clear seven feet, with nothing under five feet counted at all.
Now picture the housing stock here. The half-finished rec room in a Bridgeton ranch. The walkout lower level cut into a hillside lot in Ballwin or Des Peres, with real windows and a patio door. The story-and-a-half capes all over south city, Overland and Maplewood with knee walls upstairs. All of it is usable, lived-in space. None of it is gross living area. It goes on its own line in the sales comparison grid at a much smaller number per square foot than the space above grade. Fannie Mae even warns appraisers that MLS and assessor square footage may not have been derived using ANSI at all.
One distinction saves people real money: an appraisal is not a home inspection and never was. The appraiser forms an opinion of value and flags conditions that affect it or that loan guidelines require repaired. Nobody is running the furnace through a cycle or scoping the sewer lateral. Condition is a separate hire — and a surprising amount sits outside a standard inspection too, which is the subject of home inspections in St. Louis and what they miss.
### How long does a home appraisal take?
The visit is usually an hour or two for an ordinary single-family house. The report is what takes time, and the VA publishes real deadlines against the same local appraiser pool everyone else draws from. On the table effective May 1, 2026, VA appraisals are due within 10 business days statewide in Missouri, tightening to 9 in Jackson, St. Charles and St. Louis counties. Illinois is 10 business days statewide, and 7 in Cook, DuPage and Lake.
Conventional lenders do not publish turn times, so read those as the shape of the market rather than a promise about your file. Rural comps, a complex property or a busy spring stretch it. So does a locked room, because a report the appraiser has to qualify with an assumption often means a second trip.
Once the report exists it has a shelf life. FHA extended the initial appraisal validity period from 120 days to 180 days from the effective date of the report in Mortgagee Letter 2022-11, issued July 12, 2022, with an update stretching it to one year. And under 12 CFR 1002.14 your copy has to reach you at least three business days before closing, which is your window to read it rather than skim it at the table.
The form itself has a hard cutover date. Under the Uniform Appraisal Dataset redesign, UAD 3.6 is mandatory for all new appraisal reports submitted to the Uniform Collateral Data Portal on or after November 2, 2026, retiring Form 1004 and 70 and the rest of the legacy set in favor of one dynamic report.
Unrelated, and we know it — that inherited sideboard has a market: antique dealers.
### What happens if the appraisal comes in low?
The lender lends against the appraised value, not your contract price, so a low appraisal opens a cash gap somebody has to close. Five real moves: renegotiate the price down, split the difference, bring the gap in cash, request a reconsideration of value, or walk away if your contract gives you that right.
It is not rare. The Federal Housing Finance Agency’s Uniform Appraisal Dataset aggregate statistics, in an FHFA post published November 2, 2022, reported that nationally in 2021, 15.2 percent of appraisals came in below the contract price, 26.7 percent matched it, and 58.1 percent came in above. 2021 was a fast market where closed comps lagged live offers, so read that as a high-water figure rather than today’s rate.
A reconsideration of value is a request back through the lender asking the appraiser to look again, and it runs on facts. On July 18, 2024 five federal agencies — the OCC, the Federal Reserve, the FDIC, the NCUA and the CFPB — issued final interagency guidance on reconsiderations of value of residential real estate valuations, directing institutions to run a clear, consistent, nondiscriminatory ROV process. What moves one: a comparable sale that closed and was not used, a wrong gross living area, a wrong room count, a condition rating that ignores a documented renovation. What does not: needing the number to be higher.
Your protection depends on your loan. FHA requires the amendatory clause in the purchase contract; HUD’s model language says the buyer is not obligated to complete the purchase or forfeit earnest money unless given a written statement of appraised value of at least the stated amount, while keeping the option to proceed anyway. VA requires an escape clause under 38 CFR 36.4303(k)(4) with the same effect. On a conventional loan there is no federal clause — your protection is the appraisal contingency your contract actually contains, and the two states use different standard forms. Read yours, and find the deadline for objecting in writing.
Sellers have fewer levers, but real ones: hold your price and let the buyer bring cash, meet in the middle, take the lower number, or relist. Nothing in an appraisal obligates you to reduce the price, and nothing obligates the buyer’s lender to lend against a number its appraiser did not support.
### Is an appraisal the same as a CMA or the assessor’s value?
No, and the statutes draw the line themselves. Since July 1, 1999 it has been unlawful under section 339.501 RSMo to act as a real estate appraiser in Missouri without a license or certificate — and that same section specifically exempts a licensed real estate broker or salesperson preparing a comparative market analysis or a broker price opinion. Illinois takes the same position: under the Real Estate Appraiser Licensing Act of 2002, developing a real estate appraisal without a license is a Class A misdemeanor for a first offense.
So the three numbers people conflate are three different products. An appraisal is a credentialed opinion of market value developed under professional standards, defensible, and paid for. A CMA or broker price opinion is an agent’s pricing opinion built from comparable listings and sales — free, fast, genuinely useful for setting a list price, and legally not an appraisal. An assessed value is a tax figure produced by a formula, and in both states the formula guarantees it is not market value.
In Missouri, residential real property is assessed at 19 percent of true value in money under section 137.115 RSMo, with values set as of January 1 of each odd-numbered year. That makes 2025 and 2027 reassessment years. The ratio ignores price tier — Sunset Hills and St. Ann run through the same county assessor at the same 19 percent. St. Louis City assesses separately, so Dogtown and Webster Groves are handled by two different offices under one statute.
In Illinois, every county except Cook assesses at 33 1/3 percent of fair cash value, and the Illinois Department of Revenue derives that level from sales ratio studies covering the three most recent years before the assessment year. In Madison, St. Clair and Monroe counties — Troy included — your assessed value is anchored to a rolling three-year window of past sales, so it lags a moving market by design, in both directions. Cross the river and the ratio, the timing and the appeal body all change.
Multiplying either number back out does not produce an appraisal. Those ratios sit on a mass-appraisal estimate built without anyone walking through your kitchen. A wrong assessment is a tax appeal to your county Board of Equalization in Missouri or Board of Review in Illinois, deadline printed on the notice. A wrong lender value is a reconsideration of value. Separate fights, separate venues.
### How do you check that an appraiser is licensed in Missouri or Illinois?
Look them up on the state’s own license search, which takes a minute and costs nothing. Missouri appraisers are credentialed by the Real Estate Appraisers Commission, part of the Division of Professional Registration in the Department of Commerce and Insurance, under Chapter 339 RSMo; its licensee search runs at mopro.mo.gov. Illinois appraisers are licensed by the Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation, whose License Look Up sits on idfpr.illinois.gov.
The tiers differ slightly. Missouri issues trainee, state-licensed, certified residential and certified general credentials, renewed on a two-year cycle expiring June 30 of even-numbered years. Illinois issues associate real estate trainee appraiser, state certified residential and state certified general, overseen by a Real Estate Appraisal Administration and Disciplinary Board. On a house loan, certified residential is the credential you will usually see.
There is a federal cross-check too. The Appraisal Subcommittee maintains the National Registry of state-credentialed appraisers and registered appraisal management companies at asc.gov, searchable by name or credential number. States submit updates at least monthly, and the ASC states plainly that it has not independently verified what the states send — so treat the state site as the primary check and the registry as the backstop.
The standards are national. Appraisers working federally related transactions must comply with the Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice, adopted by the Appraisal Standards Board of The Appraisal Foundation. The current edition took effect January 1, 2024 and carries no fixed expiration. Worth noticing that this is not true of every trade at your closing — Missouri licenses appraisers, and does not license home inspectors at all.
### What can you tell an appraiser, and what crosses the line?
You can give an appraiser facts. You cannot give them a target. The valuation independence rule at 12 CFR 1026.42 prohibits anyone with an interest in the transaction from coercing, bribing or attempting to influence an appraiser’s opinion of value, and a homeowner counts. Permit dates and improvement costs are information. “I need $415,000 for this to work” is pressure.
The Appraisal Institute’s consumer guidance suggests asking your lender for permission to accompany the appraiser and to pass along anything you consider important. Worth having ready: permits and dates for the kitchen or bath remodel, the year the roof went on, the sewer lateral receipt, the finished-basement permit, an HOA fee schedule, and any genuinely comparable nearby sale that might not be in MLS — an estate sale, a family transfer, a for-sale-by-owner on your street.
What does not help: a deep clean, fresh flowers, staging. Appraisers are not scoring housekeeping. Access is what matters. Open the attic hatch, the crawlspace, the electrical panel, the furnace room and every bedroom, and clear a path to each. A room the appraiser cannot enter becomes a second visit or a report qualified with an assumption, and both cost you days.
Budget time for repairs, too. If the report conditions the value on something being fixed — peeling paint on a pre-1978 house under FHA, a missing handrail, an inoperable furnace — that work usually has to be done and re-certified before the loan funds. Learning that three days out is how closings get rescheduled.
### What this looks like from the appraiser’s side of the clipboard
Most residential orders do not come from your lender directly. They arrive through an appraisal management company that keeps a share of the fee you paid and pushes the assignment to a panel, often as a broadcast several appraisers answer at once, competing on fee and turn time. Regulation Z requires the fee appraiser be paid a customary and reasonable rate for that geographic market, and the size of the split is the standing argument in the trade. Volume swings with rates: refinances flood in when rates drop and vanish when they rise, leaving a purchase-only year where spring and early summer carry the calendar. Fannie Mae retired the phrase “appraisal waiver” on September 3, 2025 in favor of value acceptance and widened eligibility, and every waived loan is an assignment that no longer exists. Then there’s UAD 3.6, mandatory for reports submitted on or after November 2, 2026, which retires the report everyone learned to write. Private work — estates, divorce, tax appeals, pre-listing opinions — comes from people searching locally, and a complete, findable listing is how those calls start.
Need a value nobody is going to argue with? Browse real estate appraisers across the St. Louis metro on St Louis Near Me Directory, then call two certified residential appraisers, tell each the purpose - estate, divorce, tax appeal, pre-listing - and ask for the fee and the turn time in writing.
If you’re the certified appraiser people call when the number has to hold up, list your practice so they can find you.
If the real question is pricing rather than valuation, that is advice work, and it is covered in what a real estate consultant does and what it costs.
If the number that looks wrong came from the assessor rather than an appraiser, here is how to appeal your property assessment in St. Louis County.
### Frequently asked questions
### Q. What is the typical cost of an appraisal in Missouri?
A.  No state agency publishes a Missouri average. The firmest public number is a federal ceiling: on the VA appraisal fee and timeliness table effective May 1, 2026, the maximum single-family appraisal fee in Missouri is $700, with $750 for manufactured homes and $850 for two-to-four units. That is a VA cap, not a conventional average. Your binding number sits in Section B of your Loan Estimate.
### Q. What is the average cost of a real estate appraisal?
A.  No government agency or appraiser trade body publishes a verified national average, and cost-comparison sites rely on self-reported figures. Published ceilings are firmer ground: the VA table effective May 1, 2026 caps single-family appraisal fees at $700 in Missouri and $650 in Illinois. Complexity drives the real price — acreage, an unusual floor plan, a multi-unit building, a rush request.
### Q. What should I do before an appraiser comes to my house?
A.  Open everything and gather paperwork. Unlatch the attic hatch, crawlspace, electrical panel, furnace room and every bedroom, and clear a path to each. Collect permits and dates for major work, the roof’s age, the sewer lateral receipt and any HOA schedule. Skip the deep clean; it changes nothing. Ask your lender whether you may accompany the appraiser, which the Appraisal Institute suggests.
### Q. What not to say to an appraiser?
A.  Do not name the number you need. The valuation independence rule at 12 CFR 1026.42 bars anyone with an interest in the transaction from coercing, bribing or attempting to influence an appraiser’s opinion of value, and that includes the homeowner. Facts are welcome: permit dates, what the remodel cost, a nearby sale you believe is comparable. A target price is not a fact.
### Q. What devalues a home appraisal?
A.  Deferred maintenance, functional problems, and square footage that does not count. Under the ANSI Z765-2021 standard Fannie Mae has required since April 1, 2022, any space partly or fully below grade is reported as basement area, not gross living area — so a finished St. Louis basement is adjusted on its own line, at far less than upstairs space. Roof age and an inoperable furnace pull it down too.
### Q. What are the red flags for home appraisals?
A.  Read the report for factual errors first: wrong gross living area, wrong bedroom or bathroom count, a condition rating that ignores a documented renovation, comparables pulled from too far away or too far back, or a recent sale on your block that was never used. Those are the grounds for a reconsideration of value, and five federal agencies issued final interagency ROV guidance on July 18, 2024.
### Q. Is there a downside to getting your house appraised?
A.  Three of them. You pay up front, and the fee is not refunded because you dislike the result. On a purchase, a value below contract price opens a cash gap the lender will not cover. On a refinance, a low value can drop you out of the loan-to-value tier you were counting on, changing your rate or keeping mortgage insurance.
### Q. Is there a way to get a free appraisal?
A.  Not a real appraisal, but two free alternatives exist. Fannie Mae’s value acceptance — the term that replaced “appraisal waiver” on September 3, 2025 — can eliminate the appraisal on eligible loans, so there is no fee at all. And a licensed broker’s comparative market analysis costs nothing; section 339.501 RSMo exempts it from appraiser licensing precisely because it is not an appraisal.
### Q. What’s the cheapest way to get your house appraised?
A.  For a mortgage, the cheapest outcome is no appraisal at all: ask whether your loan qualifies for value acceptance, which removes the fee entirely. Failing that, desktop and hybrid options cost less than a full interior inspection where the lender allows them. For a private purpose you pick the appraiser yourself, so get written quotes from more than one.
### Q. How much money does an appraiser make per appraisal?
A.  Less than you paid, whenever an appraisal management company sits in the middle. You pay one fee; the AMC keeps a share for managing the assignment and passes the rest to the appraiser doing the work. Regulation Z at 12 CFR 1026.42(f) requires the fee appraiser be paid a customary and reasonable rate for that geographic market. No agency publishes the split, and it varies by company and assignment.

## What to Know About Cannabis Dispensaries in St. Louis
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/blog/what-to-know-about-cannabis-dispensaries-in-st-louis
Imagine it’s a Wednesday in October and your brother-in-law is in from out of state for a wedding in Manchester. On the drive in he passed a plain gray storefront with a security camera over the door and no windows, and now he wants to know whether that was really a legal weed store. It was. There is probably one within fifteen minutes of wherever you are standing in this metro.
Then he starts asking the questions you can’t actually answer. Does his out-of-state license work? How much can he buy? Can he ride back across the Poplar Street Bridge to the hotel in Fairview Heights with it in the console? Why did the receipt in Berkeley look nothing like the receipt his friend got in Belleville? And somebody at the table swears the federal government legalized the whole thing this spring, which is not quite what happened.
So here is the reference-desk version, as the rules stand on August 21, 2026, with the source named for every legal claim. No product talk, no recommendations, no opinions about whether any of this is a good idea. Just what the two states on either side of the Mississippi actually require, where they differ, and where federal law still runs straight through the middle of St. Louis.
### What are the current cannabis regulations in Missouri?
Adults 21 and older may buy and possess up to three ounces of dried, unprocessed marijuana or the equivalent, from a state-licensed dispensary, with a valid government-issued photo ID. That comes from Article XIV, Section 2 of the Missouri Constitution, added when voters passed Amendment 3 on November 8, 2022. The Division of Cannabis Regulation inside the Missouri Department of Health and Senior Services runs the program.
The transaction cap and the possession cap are the same number. Missouri’s own consumer guidance states that up to three ounces may be purchased in a single transaction and that consumers may be in possession of up to three ounces at any time (Missouri DHSS, Division of Cannabis Regulation). There is no separate, smaller limit for visitors from other states — Missouri writes the rule around age, not residency.
Two prohibitions in the constitutional text catch people out. Smoking in a public place, outside an area specifically licensed for it, carries a civil penalty of up to one hundred dollars. And consuming marijuana while operating — or being in physical control of — a motor vehicle, train, aircraft or motorboat is prohibited outright, as is smoking in one while it is being operated (Missouri Constitution, Article XIV, Section 2). Impaired driving law applies on top of that.
Home cultivation is legal in Missouri but not casual. The constitution allows up to six flowering plants, six nonflowering plants over fourteen inches, and six clones under fourteen inches, and only for a person registered with the department for cultivation. That registration is a real card you apply for, not a formality you assume.
### What are the regulations for dispensaries in Illinois?
Illinois legalized adult use through the Cannabis Regulation and Tax Act (410 ILCS 705), effective January 1, 2020, and licenses retail stores as “dispensing organizations” through the Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation. Buyers must be 21 with a government-issued ID, and Illinois — unlike Missouri — sets two different possession limits depending on whether you live there.
Those limits just doubled. Governor Pritzker signed Public Act 104-0463 (SB 3222) on June 12, 2026, and IDFPR’s own fact sheet dated June 23, 2026 spells out the change: for Illinois residents, cannabis flower went from 30 grams to 60 grams, infused products from 500 milligrams of THC to 1,000 milligrams, and concentrate from 5 grams to 10 grams. For out-of-state visitors, the caps went from 15 grams to 30 grams of flower, 250 to 500 milligrams of THC in infused products, and 2.5 to 5 grams of concentrate.
Several other operating rules changed the same day, which is why an Illinois store may look different than it did last year. Dispensaries may now offer curbside pickup and drive-through service after IDFPR reviews their plans, may hire their own security guards instead of contracting a third-party firm, may store 60 days of camera footage rather than 90, and may stay open until 2 a.m. with local municipal approval (IDFPR SB 3222 fact sheet, June 23, 2026).
Home growing is where the two states split hardest. In Illinois, only registered qualifying medical cannabis patients may grow, and the limit is five plants (Illinois cannabis program FAQ). A non-patient adult in Belleville cannot legally grow a plant that a registered adult in Affton can grow six of. Same river, opposite answer.
### Why does the same purchase cost more on one side of the river?
Because the two states stack taxes in completely different ways. Missouri charges a 6% state tax on adult-use retail sales, and local governments may add a sales tax of up to 3% (Missouri Constitution, Article XIV, Section 2). Illinois runs a tiered excise tax instead: 10% of the purchase price for cannabis with an adjusted THC level at or below 35%, 25% for anything above 35%, and 20% for cannabis-infused products, and that sits on top of the general merchandise sales tax rate in that jurisdiction (Illinois Department of Revenue).
Illinois then lets local governments layer on more. Municipalities may impose a cannabis retailers’ occupation tax up to 3%, and counties may impose up to 3% inside municipalities and up to 3.75% in unincorporated areas, all in quarter-percent increments (Illinois Department of Revenue, Informational Bulletin FY 2026-06). In other words, an Illinois county tax and a city tax can both apply to the same sale.
Missouri used to work that way too, and then it didn’t. On July 22, 2025, the Missouri Supreme Court ruled 6-1 in a case brought by a Florissant dispensary against St. Louis County that a county may impose its 3% marijuana tax only in unincorporated areas — not inside an incorporated city, town or village that levies its own. Judge Russell wrote that in an incorporated area the “local government” is the city, and in an unincorporated area it is the county (Missouri Supreme Court, July 22, 2025; reported by St. Louis Public Radio). Three percentage points came off the receipt in places like Florissant. The county 3% still applies where there is no municipality to charge it.
### What happens when you walk into a dispensary?
You show a valid government-issued photo ID at the door, every single visit, before you get past the lobby. Staff check age first and everything else second. Then you order at a counter or a kiosk, the sale is recorded in the state’s seed-to-sale tracking system against your legal limit, you pay, and you leave with a sealed, labeled package.
The ID check is not theater and it is not negotiable at the clerk’s discretion — the store’s license depends on it. Expect a security guard. Illinois now requires that guards be present at all times the store is open, whether they are contracted or employed directly (IDFPR, June 2026). Expect cameras. Expect the lobby to be a separate room from the sales floor.
Consumption is not part of the visit at a typical store. Illinois does allow individual municipalities to authorize on-premises consumption at a licensed dispensary, so it genuinely varies town to town on that side of the river; assume no unless the store says otherwise. And on the Missouri side, Article XIV’s public-place restriction means the parking lot is not a solution.
### Why is it cash or debit at almost every dispensary?
Because federal banking rules have not caught up with state law, and the card networks wrote their own prohibitions on top. Visa, Mastercard and American Express each bar cannabis transactions under their own operating rules, which is why the terminal at the register runs PIN debit or an on-site ATM rather than a normal credit swipe. Federally insured banks that do serve the industry take on Bank Secrecy Act and anti-money-laundering obligations to do it.
Congress has repeatedly tried and repeatedly not finished. The SAFE Banking Act — the bill that would shield banks serving state-legal cannabis businesses — was reintroduced in both chambers in 2026 after clearing the Senate Banking Committee back in 2023, and it has still not become law. Nothing about the April 2026 rescheduling order changes that on its own; it did not create a banking safe harbor.
The practical consequence for a shopper is small and annoying: bring cash or a PIN debit card, expect an ATM fee, and expect the register to round the transaction. The consequence for the business is much larger, because a cash-heavy retailer has to pay for armored pickups, a vault and counting procedure that a coffee shop never thinks about.
Wildly off topic — your yard still needs a landscaping crew.
### Is marijuana still illegal under federal law?
Mostly, yes — and the part that changed is narrower than the headlines suggested. On April 28, 2026, a final order published at 91 Fed. Reg. 22714 moved two specific categories from Schedule I to Schedule III of the Controlled Substances Act: marijuana contained in an FDA-approved drug product, and marijuana subject to a state medical marijuana license. Everything else, including adult-use product sold in a state-legal dispensary, stayed in Schedule I.
A separate and much broader proceeding is still open. The DEA held a formal administrative hearing beginning June 29, 2026 on whether marijuana generally should move to Schedule III, and post-hearing briefs were due August 17, 2026. No final order on that broader question had issued as of this writing. Even if it does, Schedule III is not legalization — it is a controlled substance with a prescription requirement.
Three consequences are worth stating plainly, because they surprise people in a two-state metro. Carrying cannabis across a state line is a federal offense, and that includes every bridge over the Mississippi between here and Illinois; a legal Missouri purchase does not become a legal Illinois possession by driving it there, and neither state’s limits travel with you. Federal property is federal jurisdiction regardless of what the state says, and downtown St. Louis contains Gateway Arch National Park, a unit of the National Park Service, plus federal courthouses and VA facilities. And safety-sensitive transportation workers are still covered by federal drug testing rules — the U.S. Department of Transportation posted on February 25, 2026 that it is “still unacceptable for people who work in safety-sensitive transportation positions to use marijuana,” and 49 CFR Part 40 has not changed. There is no medical-card exception for a CDL holder. If that describes your work, our post on what to know before buying a commercial truck in St. Louis covers the rest of that world.
One area is genuinely unsettled and we are not going to pretend otherwise. Federal law bars an “unlawful user” of a controlled substance from possessing a firearm under 18 U.S.C. 922(g)(3), and ATF’s firearms transaction form has long asked buyers to certify on that point. After the April 2026 order, ATF circulated a draft revision to that form, and the Justice Department has said the rescheduling order does not by itself rewrite the criminal statute. If you own firearms, treat this as an open legal question and ask an attorney rather than a website. Employment protections are similarly state-specific and still being litigated in both states.
### Where is cannabis still off limits around St. Louis?
Public places, vehicles, federal land, and any property whose owner says no. Missouri’s constitution attaches a civil penalty of up to one hundred dollars to smoking in a public place outside a licensed area, and prohibits consuming or smoking in a motor vehicle, train, aircraft or motorboat while it is being operated (Article XIV, Section 2). Illinois prohibits use in public places, in vehicles, on school grounds, in state and local government buildings, and near anyone under 21 who is not a registered medical patient (Illinois cannabis program FAQ).
Landlords, employers and hotels are their own jurisdictions. Neither state’s law obligates a private property owner to permit smoking, and lease language routinely bans it the same way it bans tobacco. A hotel in Maryland Heights or St. Charles can and often does charge a cleaning fee. Nothing in either state’s legalization changed a property owner’s right to set that rule.
Local government still shapes where stores exist at all. In Missouri, a city or county can only prohibit non-medical dispensary facilities by putting it to voters, and it takes at least 60% approval at a general election in a presidential election year (Missouri Constitution, Article XIV, Section 2) — a deliberately high bar. In Illinois, units of local government have broader zoning and time, place and manner authority over cannabis businesses (410 ILCS 705/55-25), which is why dispensaries cluster in some Metro East municipalities and are absent from their neighbors.
### Does a Missouri medical marijuana card still get you anything?
Yes, three things, and they are real. Tax: medical purchases are taxed at 4% rather than the 6% adult-use rate.
